- When sentiment shows strong positive change followed by a spike, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is consistently negative or flat over 3+ days, model often underestimates downside risk — add 2–5% buffer to forecast.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overcorrects downward — adjust downward forecast by 3–8% to avoid premature reversal.
- If news volume is high and sentiment is positive, model often overestimates price — cap forecast at 1.5–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or declining, model tends to lag behind true price — forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% to capture momentum.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows — if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5%.
- When sentiment change is negative and news volume is low, model underestimates volatility — add 1–3% volatility buffer to forecast range.
